To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inactivation of trytpohan indole-lysae by trifluoroalnine is prevented by indole, which is consistent with a catalytically-competent species, the beta,beta difluoro alpha amino acrylate intermediate, being the inactivating species.
indole protects tryptopphan indole-lyases, but not trytpohan synthase, against trifluoroalanin-induced inactivation.
indole protects tryptaphan indole-lysae from inactivation by the mechanism-based inactivators trifluoroalanin and 2-bromopyruvic acid.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of mechanism-based inactivators of enzymes.
the inactivation of enzymes by trifluoroacetone, trifluoroalanin...
the mechanism by which tryptophan is formed by tryptophanase and tryptophan synthesis from indole and pyruvate by tryptophansynthase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

inactivation of the tryptophanylase by TFA occurs by an intermediate, the beta,beta'-difluoro-alpha-amioacrylate which can react with indole, a natural inhibitor, or water to yield products or be trapped by the enzyme to form the inactivated species.

the protection of tryptaphan indole- lyase by indole is a result of the ability of indole to react with the difluoro-alpha-aminoaacylate intermediate of the reaction, thus preventing its conversion to an inactive enzyme.
inactivation of the enzyme by trifluoroalanylalanine is due to a mechanism in which the enzyme is converted to an inactive form by a reactive intermediate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tryptophanyl-tRNA synthetase from E. coli is not inactivated by trifluoroalanyl-AMP, and that tryptophanyl-AMP is not formed from tryptophan and trifluoroalanyladenylate.
the inactivation of trytophan indole-lyases and tryptophan syntheses by mechanism-based inhibitors are different.

indole is an effective competitive inhibitor for tryptophan synthesis by both tryptophanase and tryptophan-synthase, but only tryptophan-ase can be inactivated by trifluoro-alanine, and only tryptophanease inactivation is protected by indole.
The main takeaway from our work is that
indole is a good nucleophile and that the enzyme can form a covalent bond with indole.
the enzyme can form the beta,beta- difluoro-alpha-amidoacrylate intermediate in the absence of a substrate.
indole is an effective mechanism-based inactivating agent of tryptophyl-tRNA synthetase.
